$comment: Anatomy manifest of the RequirementReviewer agent (exemplar). Paths are relative to the repository root. Check it with: python design_lab.py dissect

agent.name: RequirementReviewer
agent.owner: Trainee A and Trainee B (QE pair)
agent.job: Turns one user story into grounded requirement findings, each with one clarifying question, as JSON.
agent.autonomy_note: Level 2: fixed path, one model call per story, no tools; a tester reviews every finding and the product owner answers the questions.

parts.name: Model (LLM)
parts.job: Reads text and writes text. The only non-deterministic part. Kept swappable.

parts.name: Instructions (system message)
parts.job: Standing orders: role, goal, scope, process, rules, output, uncertainty, boundaries, style. Same every run.

parts.name: Prompt template (user message)
parts.job: Fixed wording plus $placeholders filled with this story's data. Says 'here is today's job'.

parts.name: Input contract (preconditions)
parts.job: What the agent accepts. Bad input is rejected before a model call is paid for.

parts.name: Output contract (postconditions)
parts.job: What the agent returns: shape, types, patterns, enums, a version and an honest 'I can't' path.
parts.owner: Agent designers, agreed with consumers (question log, test design agent)

parts.name: Validation rules (rule catalogue)
parts.job: Rules a schema cannot see because they compare output with input: R1-R7, plus warnings Q1-Q2 and human Q3.
parts.built: today: catalogue + R2, R4, R6 examples; full script Friday

parts.name: Validation gate
parts.job: Applies input schema, output schema and rules to every run. Rejects, never silently passes on.

parts.name: Tools
parts.job: Functions the agent may call. RequirementReviewer v1.0.0 has none on purpose: the story is handed to it.

parts.name: Context and memory
parts.job: Context = instructions + rendered template. Memory = nothing. Every run starts fresh, so it is easy to test.

parts.name: Orchestration runtime
parts.job: Runs the loop: check input, render, call model, parse, validate, hand to a human, log.
parts.built: Friday (anatomy_lab.py shows the pieces separately today)

parts.name: Logs
parts.job: One record per run: versions of instructions, template and contract, sizes, errors, timings.

parts.name: Sample input/output pairs
parts.job: Reviewed worked examples: spec by example, few-shot, golden regression data, contract test data.

parts.name: Human reviewer
parts.job: Judges meaning: correct, complete, grounded. Signs off. Accountable; the AI never is.
parts.owner: Story's tester; product owner answers the questions

boundaries.can_go_wrong: story_id '420'; no acceptance criteria; unknown field 'reviewer_mood'; max_findings 50
$focus left unfilled; the wrong story inserted
'make reasonable assumptions' leads the model to answer its own questions ('2 seconds')
prose or a code fence around the JSON; truncated reply
status 'done'; id 'F-1'; question without '?'; missing quote
quote not in the story; cites AC6 of a 5-AC story; 12 findings when max_findings is 6
a finding that is technically grounded but irrelevant; a real problem missed (shipping and tax)
a model update changes the findings; nobody can tell which instructions version produced a log
instructions 1.1.0 stop flagging 'quickly'; nobody notices without the pairs

design_questions.question: Can its job be stated in one sentence without 'and'?
design_questions.answer: Turns one user story into grounded requirement findings, each with one clarifying question, as JSON.

design_questions.question: Assistant, workflow or autonomous agent? Is that justified?
design_questions.answer: Workflow (level 2): fixed path, one model call, a human reviews every finding. Requirements review starts narrow.

design_questions.question: Where are the instructions stored? Versioned? Do they say what to do when the input is unclear?
design_questions.answer: agent/instructions.md, Version 1.0.0, nine sections; 'ask, never answer' rule with a reason.

design_questions.question: Which parts of the prompt change per request, and how are they filled?
design_questions.answer: Five $placeholders filled once with string.Template.substitute; max_findings and focus defaults from the input schema.

design_questions.question: What does it accept? What happens to bad input?
design_questions.answer: rr_input.schema.json; bad input rejected before any model call (P04).

design_questions.question: Is the output machine-checkable? Versioned? Is there a way to say 'I can't'?
design_questions.answer: rr_output.schema.json; contract_version const 1.0.0; status needs_clarification + open_questions.

design_questions.question: What is checked automatically? What rules does the schema not cover?
design_questions.answer: S1, S2 by schema; R1-R7 in code (Friday); Q1-Q2 warnings; Q3 human. Catalogue says where each lives.

design_questions.question: Which tools can it call, and could any change something (write, delete, send)?
design_questions.answer: None. The story is passed in; nothing is written anywhere.

design_questions.question: What does the model see on each call? Is anything kept between runs?
design_questions.answer: Instructions + rendered template. Stateless: nothing kept between runs.

design_questions.question: Could you explain any given run a week later?
design_questions.answer: Planned for Friday: one record per run with instructions, template and contract versions.

design_questions.question: Who approves the output, and where is that recorded?
design_questions.answer: The story's tester reviews findings (Wednesday checklist); the product owner answers the questions.

design_questions.question: Are there sample input/output pairs that show correct behaviour?
design_questions.answer: P01-P06: happy path, two edge cases, clarification, invalid input, out of scope.
